bill.title: A bill to amend the Leahy-Smith America Invents Act to limit intellectual property protection for plants, and for other purposes.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would amend the America Invents Act to restrict intellectual property protections for plants. The source material provides only the title, so the specific changes to plant-related patents, plant variety protections, or other IP mechanisms cannot be determined without the bill text.

industries.rationale: The bill directly addresses intellectual property protection for plants, which affects seed companies, plant breeders, and agricultural producers who rely on or are subject to plant patents and variety protections.
Pharmaceutical and biotech companies that develop plant-derived compounds or use plant genetics in drug development may be affected by changes to plant IP protections.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
